focus.rationale: T16 re-derivation (2026-09-11), value CHANGED from `general`. A dedicated repair route now exists — R2 = `candidate` (§7.10, via the T16 tail-marker-implausible relief) — so §10.2's `repair` row (R2 ∈ {candidate, tested}, and nothing else, T13a) qualifies for the first time on this record. `smoothing` is re-checked and still does not qualify: this pass's T16 relief is scoped to R2 alone (per the ruling's stated consequence), so SFR/`smoothing_route` is left exactly as it was — `moderate`, one observation only, because §7.4.1 clause 3's below-marker treatment of the candidate second (lubrication) route is not re-opened here — and §7.4.1's two-observation test still fails outright. `repair` is therefore the sole qualifying route in the rank order (repair > smoothing > curl_definition > heat_styling > detangling > volume_lightness > shine); it becomes `primary` without needing a tie-break. The C2 marketing position is repair-led ('Anti-Snap', 'reduziert Haarbruch und Spliss', 'bis zu 96% stärker') and corroborates the now-qualifying formula route, but it does not create it (principle 4, §10.2 step 5) — the route already clears on R2 alone. Every other route still fails its own gate exactly as before: curl_definition (HOLD none), heat_styling (application_stage [towel_dry], no pre_heat), detangling (no C1/C2 positioning), volume_lightness (WT moderate), shine (would restate the film). No secondary focus: nothing else clears its own independent-support bar. Result: repair, still uncertain — this record's values remain broadly uncertain from the rank-3 marker, now formally `tail_marker_implausible` (§3.1.1, T16) rather than the retired `candidate_below_tail` reading.
focus.derivation: §10.2: qualifying routes are collected beyond baseline conditioning (§10.2.1, permissive reading T13b), then the rank order repair > smoothing > curl_definition > heat_styling > detangling > volume_lightness > shine binds.

§10.2 principle 4: official positioning may corroborate a route but never creates one.
limitations: A focus is a statement of distinctive purpose, not an efficacy claim or a measured endpoint.
